records.package_tree_identity_basis: git tree SHA of the package directory at the pin, read from a full clone with git ls-tree

records.package_license_finding: root MIT only (LICENSE b4625e9b, 'Copyright (c) 2026 Daniel'); no package-level LICENSE/NOTICE. catalogue.mjs states all micro-examples are original MIT material; SOURCES lists Gutenberg public-domain works and contemporary publisher works (Wuxiaworld, Yen Press, Webnovel) as bibliographic URLs only with 'No text is bundled' - no copied third-party text found.
records.dependencies: Node >=22.14 (dependency-free), local writable filesystem; installed 'novel-craft' binary (npm package or node cli/index.mjs); optional authenticated OpenAI Codex CLI or a user-supplied JSON stdin/stdout runner command for inner-agent generation; no API keys bundled.
records.purpose_and_nontrigger: Drives a bundled local CLI to create, continue, revise, review and export webnovel manuscripts with proposal/commit state and quote-backed canon facts. Not for non-fiction or one-off prose without a project workspace; does not authorize publishing, scraping protected chapters, credential storage, or committing proposals/accepting canon without writer authority.
records.content_finding: A well-engineered, safety-conscious local manuscript tool: proposal/commit with revision expectations, quote-grounded canon and reviews, no-overwrite exports and explicit untrusted-content framing. Main gaps are that SKILL.md assumes the CLI is installed and omits runtime prerequisites, and literary effectiveness is unevidenced; the optional Codex runner sends manuscript content to the user's chosen provider.
records.bundled_file_findings: index.mjs: argument parsing/dispatch, strict per-command flags, exclusive output files (0600, 'wx'). store.mjs: content-addressed objects, immutable revisions, lock file, journaled transactions with recovery, undo; unlinks only its own LOCK/transaction files and manuscript files per journal. runner.mjs: spawns codex exec (read-only sandbox, ephemeral) or a user-supplied command with shell:false, timeout/output caps, tmpdir cleanup. generate.mjs: plan->draft->review->revise loop with call budget and checkpoints, ends in one proposal. context.mjs: budgeted context packet with POV fact filtering and coverage warnings. checks.mjs/schemas.mjs: literal checks and schema validation requiring excerpt/quote grounding. export.mjs: md/html/epub (custom store-only ZIP), HTML-escaped. catalogue.mjs (38.7 KB, read in full): ~50 genre profiles with original micro-examples plus bibliographic SOURCES (craft essays, ACL papers, Gutenberg and publisher URLs, checked_at 2026-09-07); content guardrails (non-graphic adult only, no sexualising minors). verify-package.mjs: dev-time npm pack/offline install check in tmpdir. test/: node:test suites with a deterministic fixture runner; temp dirs only, no network.
records.authority_and_privacy_finding: Consequential actions are local file writes in the user's project (.novelcraft state, manuscript/chapter-NNNN.md, export files). Gate: proposals are inert until 'commit <id> --expect <rev>' within explicit or delegated authority; --accept/--accept-facts are explicit delegation flags and delegated commit is blocked when a major review finding is unresolved; undo/recover/unlock require --yes (a flag the agent could pass, but the operations are reversible/journaled). setup writes SKILL.md into .agents/skills only on explicit command and refuses to overwrite a differing file (local self-install helper, no remote fetch). Data egress: with --runner codex the full context packet (manuscript excerpts, plan, facts) is sent via the user's own Codex CLI to its model provider; SKILL.md tells the agent not to launch an inner agent when it can write directly. doctor probes 'codex --version'. No network calls in the CLI itself, no credential reads, stderr from runner is drained, not logged.
records.capability_specific: Transactional local webnovel drafting, revision, canon-fact continuity and export CLI

rubric_dimension_rationale.trigger_precision: 1/2: description covers creating, continuing, revising, continuity review and export of webnovels; 'fiction writing' is broad and overlaps the 13 sibling novel-craft-* skills with no non-trigger guidance.
rubric_dimension_rationale.procedural_clarity: 2/2: concrete command sequence (schema/status -> init -> context --chapter -> import --file -> diff -> commit --expect; review --packet; export --format md|html|epub --out) matching index.mjs COMMAND_FLAGS.
rubric_dimension_rationale.authority_safety: 2/2: all writes are local to the project workspace; generation yields a proposal, commit needs --expect revision and 'explicit or delegated writer authority'; canon facts stay candidates without --accept-facts; undo/recover/unlock require --yes; export and setup refuse to overwrite; no publishing, scraping or credential storage.
rubric_dimension_rationale.failure_handling: 2/2: checkpointed runs with generate --resume, max-calls caps, recover for interrupted transactions, unlock only for dead PIDs (store.unlock checks process.kill(pid,0)), SOURCE_CHANGED refusal instead of overwrite, typed exit codes.
rubric_dimension_rationale.evidence_discipline: 2/2: review findings must cite real excerpts (validateReview rejects absent excerpts), canon facts require verbatim supporting quotes, and the text states a successful command proves storage, not literary quality.
rubric_dimension_rationale.dependency_coherence: 1/2: the CLI implementation is bundled in the package, but SKILL.md invokes a 'novel-craft' binary on PATH with no install/run instruction (npm package or node cli/index.mjs) and omits the Node >=22.14 requirement stated only in package.json/HELP; codex runner needs an authenticated Codex CLI.
rubric_dimension_rationale.portability_honesty: 1/2: honest that the direct-writing route needs no extra model or keys and that Codex is optional, but the Node runtime, npm distribution and local filesystem requirement are not stated in SKILL.md.
rubric_dimension_rationale.usefulness_differentiation: 2/2: distinctive transactional manuscript store (content-addressed objects, revisions, proposals, receipts, undo) with quote-backed canon facts split into world/belief/reader/plan and POV filtering; not generic writing advice.
rubric_dimension_rationale.adversarial_resilience: 2/2: runner prompt marks manuscript/reference content as untrusted data and forbids tools/URLs/filesystem; no shell (shell:false); path traversal and symlink refusal in util.inside; Codex invoked with --sandbox read-only --ephemeral.
rubric_dimension_rationale.effectiveness_design: 1/2: extensive protocol/integrity tests (36 integration cases) but the fixture runner is explicitly 'not a real language model or a quality benchmark'; no evidence the prose/review loop improves fiction quality.

records.salvage: Proposal/commit-with-expected-revision pattern for agent-written prose; canon facts requiring verbatim supporting quotes and separating world/belief/reader/plan with POV filtering; review findings that must quote real excerpts plus an 'intentional reading'; no-overwrite exclusive output writes.
